html:
The Korean Armistice Agreement was signed at Panmunjom, on the border of the two Koreas, on 27 July 1953, ending the fighting of the Korean War that followed the division of Korea.

It was signed by the commanders of the United Nations forces, the North Korean army and the Chinese People's Volunteers after two years of talks, stuck mostly on whether prisoners could refuse to go home. South Korea's president refused to sign.

It set up the Demilitarized Zone, a strip about four kilometres wide across the peninsula, and a commission to watch the truce at Panmunjom. No peace treaty followed, so the two Koreas remain formally at war. The border has seen raids, shootings and tunnels, and also summits, among them the meetings of Kim Jong Un with South Korea's president and Donald Trump there in 2018 and 2019.
sum: The Korean Armistice Agreement was signed at Panmunjom, on the border of the two Koreas, on 27 July 1953, ending the fighting of the Korean War that followed the division of Korea.
